M9 — 2026-09-23
NEVER RENUMBER A TASK ID WHEN A TASK MOVES BETWEEN PHASES. An id is a handle, not a location: it is cited from other initiatives' notes, from decisions, from cross-session messages and from commit messages, none of which are updated when a plan is reorganised, so renumbering makes every existing citation silently wrong or ambiguous. A task whose id does not match its phase number is a cosmetic oddity; a citation that resolves to the wrong task, or to nothing, is a real loss. This is the same reasoning CLAUDE.md gives for citing tasks and phases by ID and never with § — a heading is a projection templates can change, the id underneath is truth. Applied 2026-09-23: self-improve 3.5 and 3.6 moved into Phase 5 and kept their ids, with the reason in that phase's note so the next reader does not tidy them. If a renumber is ever genuinely required, it needs a Decision naming the old and new ids, the way fold-parity case ids are protected (r1-fixes D21).
